text:
ana: FYI seeing a sudden spike of 502/504s on hosted /v1/generate in eu-west starting ~08:03UTC. Several customers reporting timeouts and one mentions duplicate billing events. tagging SRE/infra.
incidents-bot: ALERT: hosted-eu-west /v1/generate 5xx rate > 12% over 5m. Triggered by p95 latency surge.
devin: I'm on it — looking at ingress + runtime metrics. can someone share a repro curl?
sarah: Support reported 3 customers so far (acme-inc, finlytics, noteapp). all show request id in logs then a 504. Customer says they retried and got charged twice.
mike: I checked recent deploys: no code deploys in past 6h. infra autoscaler did a scale event at 07:58UTC. Kernel/driver updates none.
devin: Initial look — gateway timeouts correlate with high open connections on edge-proxy and a backlog on kvcache-reader. p95 queue depth on runtime up x6.
nana: (typo) sorry meant ana above
ana: repro curl from support: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> hangs then 504
jules: I can pull connection traces — routing shows traffic hitting a few overloaded pods that then marched into a longer tail.
devin: Mitigation step 1: enabled routing penalty to divert to eu-fallback-pool (smaller models) and turned on per-customer circuit breaker for the 3 impacted tenants. Done at 08:12UTC.
mike: Also bumped runtime concurrency limit on eu-hosted pool from 32->48 for 10m to drain backlog. noticed KV cache miss rate increased ~3x around spike. possible warmup storm.
sarah: Notifying customers with temporary mitigation & asking about duplicate charges. support will pause billing callbacks for affected accounts.
devin: Quick repro logs (truncated):
```
[08:03:21] gateway - req_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate backend=runtime-12 status=504 elapsed=30001ms
[08:03:22] runtime-12 - ERROR kvcache read timeout key=session-987 elapsed=1500ms
[08:03:23] runtime-12 - queue_wait=1200ms model=large-llama
```
nana: Could be a cascading warmup: large models causing long KV cache loads under sudden tenant burst.
jules: I spun up an extra pool with quantized variants (q4) and started routing ~18% of new requests there at 08:20UTC — observing p95 drop ~40% for routed traffic.
devin: Next actions (short):
- keep fallback routing enabled until kvcache miss rate < 1% and p95 stable for 10m
- create targeted alert for KV read latency > 200ms (devin)
- support to issue provisional billing hold for impacted accounts (sarah)
- infra to run KV warmup job for hot keys (mike)
- postmortem doc and timeline (jules)
sarah: support note: lodged jira INC-3187 for customer comms, billing hold request id BH-7321.
mike: running KV warmup now (script triggered at 08:35UTC) — will monitor.
devin: tl;dr root cause hypothesis: sudden tenant burst on large quantized-unfriendly model variants causing KV cache misses and runtime queueing -> gateway timeouts. Need better warmup + autoscale wiring and per-tenant backpressure.
jules: I'll own the postmortem write-up. rough ETA EOD. will include reproducer steps, timelines, and action owners.
nana: one more follow-up: investigate why billing webhook retried immediately on 504s; we should add idempotency guard in billing worker (action for billing/eng).
devin: noted. I'll add a temporary play: set billing webhook retry jitter to larger window for the next 24h.
sarah: customers notified with workaround and expected follow-up.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations applied at 08:12UTC and 08:20UTC. status=stabilizing.
jules: last check 09:05UTC: p95 back to normal for eu-hosted, KV miss rate trending down. I'll post full timeline in the postmortem.
nana: thanks team. closing this triage channel; moving to postmortem doc thread.
